violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: tomato/marinara sauce on the steam table was 125º.
violations.corrective_action: The food employee stated additional room temperature canned sauce was added to the hot sauce already in the steam table. This indicates that the sauce is being reheated in the steam table. Steam tables are not intended to reheat foods. It is intended for keeping foods that are already heated properly, hot at 135º and above. Commercially processed foods such as the sauce should be reheated to 135º on the stove, in a microwave, or other practical method, then placed in the steam table. Adding room temperature sauce to the hot sauce already in the steam sauce will lower the temperature of the hot sauce. Discontinue using the steam table to reheat foods. The EHS educated the PIC on how to properly reheat foods and to not use the steam table to reheat foods.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: tuna salad made yesterday in the right Everest 2-door prep unit was 47º. Pico de gallo in the same unit was 46º and cut lettuce was 44º. The ambient temperature of that unit was 42º. BBQ pork in the right 2-door sandwich/pizza unit was 59º, pastrami was 53º, spinach artichoke dip was 44º, cooked meatballs were 43º. The ambient temperature of the unit 50º. In the walk-in, chili was 47º, garlic chicken was 45º, sliced turkey was 49º, and sliced beef was 47º. The ambient temperature of the unit was 41º. None of these foods were recently prepared and had been in their respective units for over 4 hours.
violations.corrective_action: All the food listed above were discarded due to temperature abuse. The ambient temperatures of the refrigerators they were being stored in were too high; they need to be adjusted or serviced. Staff was aware that the sandwich/pizza prep unit was not working properly and had submitted a work order to have the unit repaired. They are waiting on a part. In the meantime, they were using ice to try and keep the food in the unit cold. However, the ice was only touching the bottoms of the storage containers and most of the foods out of temperature were stacked too high for the ice to do any good, which was why they were out of temperature. Staff reduced the amount of food in the containers. Additionally, food such as sliced meats and garlic chicken were stored in individual plastic bags and the foods may not have been properly cooled before being placed in the bags. It is important to keep TCS foods 41º and below at all times. A refrigerator that is not working properly should not be used. LOST DOG CAFE (Inspection Date: 08/12/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: chili in the walk-in made and cooled over 6 hours ago was 47º. Packages of garlic chicken, sliced turkey and slice beef prepared and cooled over 6 hours ago were 45º, 49º, and 47º, respectively. Chicken and corn chowder made today was stored covered in a large container and was 80ºF.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. Except for the chicken and corn chowder made today, all the foods listed were discarded due to temperature abuse and improper cooling. It is very important to cool foods properly. The EHS educated the kitchen staff and the PIC on how to properly cool large batches of foods by separating it in smaller batches and storing uncovered. The EHS also provided a cooling and other fact sheets to the PIC. Ensure that sliced meats and other prepared foods are cooled to 41º before storing them in plastic baggies. It is very difficult for food to cool when stored in plastic baggies.

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: There was no temperature measuring device located in the following cold or hot holding equipment: two of the prep refrigerators did not have thermometers.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. Ensure that all refrigerators have thermometers and check them routinely to ensure the units are working properly. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. The PIC corrected this during the inspection.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration units were not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: The right Everest 2-door prep unit (tuna salad, crab mix, pico store there) was not keeping foods cold enough. The ambient temperature was 40º and foods in the unit were above 41º. The right Everest 2-door prep unit (sandwich and pizza unit) was not working properly. The ambient temperature of the unit was above 41º and foods in it were above 41º. The walk-in refrigerator was not working properly. The ambient temperature of the unit was above 41º and several foods in it were not cold enough.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. All these units need to be adjusted or serviced as soon as possible. Correct as soon as possible or within 3 days. Follow-up is required for this violation. For food safety, the ambient temperature of a properly working refrigerator should be no higher than 39ºF.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. The manager cannot locate a employee health policy during the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. The EHS provided the manager with the model Fairfax County employee health policy. The manager had all employees trained and signed the form during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Waffle fries=70F, Fried onion rings =69F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19.Both items were discarded during the inspection

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. Two spray bottles that contained toxic cleaning chemicals solutions were noted to be in labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. Corrected during the inspection.

violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter. Observed wet wiping towels placed on work surfaces and not soaked in sanitizing solution in-between use.
